node-1.label: Patient presented to emergency department with severe back pain, light-headedness, and chest pain

node-2.label: Medical history includes infective endocarditis and hepatitis C secondary to ongoing intravenous drug use

node-3.label: Recently underwent tricuspid valve replacement with a 29-mm bioprosthetic Carpentier-Edwards valve, complicated by transient third-degree heart block; two days after pacemaker placement

node-4.label: Physical exam showed blood pressure 94/60 mm Hg and heart rate 150-190 beats per minute

why.why: TEE directly demonstrates pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid regurgitation due to a flail leaflet, the hallmark of active infective endocarditis; ECG grouped beating with 1:2 AV conduction also suggests perivalvular extension or ischemia. Combined with the history of IVDU, prosthetic valve, and shock, this strongly supports infective endocarditis with septic shock. Confidence is 0.75 rather than higher because blood cultures and inflammatory markers are still pending and a post-procedure complication cannot be fully excluded.

TEE identifies active endocarditis with vegetations and a flail leaflet, better explaining the hemodynamic instability; no new evidence directly supports a post-procedure complication. However, pacemaker lead vegetations and pericardial effusion were not assessed, so tamponade or bleeding cannot be fully excluded, and the recent pacemaker placement still leaves this as a plausible alternative. Confidence reduced from 0.3 to 0.2.

TEE reveals active endocarditis and no direct imaging evidence of pulmonary embolism was reported. Although IVDU and recent surgery are risk factors for thromboembolism, the acute shock presentation is better explained by infective endocarditis with septic shock, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.1.

TEE identified infective endocarditis and no imaging evidence of acute aortic syndrome was reported; the back pain is more plausibly referred from endocarditis/septic shock. With strong TEE support for endocarditis, acute aortic syndrome is much less likely, reducing confidence from 0.15 to 0.05.

node-9.label: Transesophageal echocardiography reveals pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid regurgitation due to a flail leaflet

node-10.label: ECG shows grouped beating with 1:2 AV conduction, suggesting a conduction abnormality

node-11.label: Blood cultures and inflammatory markers remain unavailable

node-12.label: Pacemaker lead vegetations and pericardial effusion were not assessed on transesophageal echocardiography

attrs.why: TEE shows pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid regurgitation, and ECG grouped beating with 1:2 AV conduction suggests a conduction abnormality that may reflect perivalvular extension or ischemia. These findings support local extension of endocarditis into the conduction system. Confidence is moderate at 0.45 because blood cultures are pending and dedicated assessment of the pacemaker lead and pericardium is still incomplete.
